stages.title: Lexical entry
stages.body: Learn headword, class, plain meaning, collocation, contrast and original sentence.

stages.title: Meaning in context
stages.body: Choose the sense licensed by the sentence, not the first dictionary gloss.

stages.title: Register
stages.body: Prefer plain contemporary formal English over ornamental or colloquial substitution.

stages.title: Collocation
stages.body: Learn words with their normal partners.

stages.title: Confusables
stages.body: Separate similar spelling or sound by meaning and grammar.

stages.title: Spelling patterns
stages.body: Use families and suffix rules while remembering genuine exceptions.

stages.title: British and American variants
stages.body: Accept consistent standard variants unless the paper specifies a house style.

stages.title: Word formation
stages.body: Use the grammatical slot to choose noun, verb, adjective or adverb.

stages.title: Synonyms
stages.body: Match denotation, intensity and register rather than treating near-synonyms as identical.

stages.title: Antonyms
stages.body: Keep the grammatical class and contextual dimension.

stages.title: Idioms and proverbs
stages.body: State conventional meaning and use the expression naturally.

stages.title: Retrieval and editing
stages.body: Use spaced recall, sentence production and a confusable log under time.
